name: Question 51
problem:
The random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability density function

$$
f(x,y)={\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{8}(x+{y}^{2}),\, & 0\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{4}$ and $\text{E}[Y]=\frac{9}{16},$ calculate the covariance of $X$ and $Y.$
worked_solution:
The covariance of $X$ and $Y$ can be calculated using the formula

$$
\text{Cov}[X,Y]=\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y].
$$

To find $\text{E}[XY],$ we use the rule of the lazy statistician:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}xyf(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}xy\cdot \frac{3}{8}(x+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{8}y{\int }_{0}^{2}({x}^{2}+x{y}^{2})\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{8}y{[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}{y}^{2}]}_{x=0}^{x=2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{3}{8}y[\frac{8}{3}+2{y}^{2}]\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(y+\frac{3}{4}{y}^{3})\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}+\frac{3}{16}{y}^{4}]}_{y=0}^{y=1} \\  & =\frac{11}{16}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the covariance formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{11}{16}-(\frac{5}{4})(\frac{9}{16}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{64}.\end{aligned}
$$

f(x,y)={38(x+y2),0≤x≤2,0≤y≤1,0,otherwise.

Given that E[X]=54 and E[Y]=916, calculate the covariance of X and Y.

Correct
EXPLANATION

The covariance of X and Y can be calculated using the formula

Cov[X,Y]=E[XY]−E[X]⋅E[Y].

To find E[XY], we use the rule of the lazy statistician:

E[XY]=∫01∫02xyf(x,y)dxdy=∫01∫02xy⋅38(x+y2)dxdy=∫0138y∫02(x2+xy2)dxdy=∫0138y[13x3+12x2y2]x=0x=2dy=∫0138y[83+2y2]dy=∫01(y+34y3)dy=[12y2+316y4]y=0y=1=1116.

Finally, using the covariance formula, we get

Cov[X,Y]=E[XY]−E[X]⋅E[Y]=1116−(54)(916)=−164.
